explainedBy: A 15-year-old walks to the library in May and never comes back.
Nobody actually searches for Ellie Mack.

shotIntent.subject: the ten years the replacements cover
shotIntent.action: the number 10 YEARS slams in, then two bars: nobody searching vs everyone holding a replacement
shotIntent.payoff: the replacements kept a secret hidden for a decade

explainedBy: Each person holds a replacement for Ellie, and those replacements hide a crime for 10 years.

storyboard.claim: The replacements hide a crime for 10 years.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A monumental 10 YEARS with two bars: searching for Ellie (empty) vs holding a replacement (full).
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Turns the hook that nobody searches into what they hold instead.
storyboard.addedInformation: Puts the ten-year span and the search-vs-replacement contrast on screen.

shotIntent.subject: who takes which replacement
shotIntent.action: three people each take a stand-in

explainedBy: Laurel takes Poppy, Noelle takes a baby, Theo takes Hanna: each a replacement.

storyboard.claim: Each person takes a replacement, not Ellie
storyboard.concreteVisual: Three columns: Laurel - Poppy, Noelle - a baby, Theo - Hanna
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Sets up the gallery
storyboard.addedInformation: Who replaces Ellie for whom

callout.text: Desperate for the copy to be real

explainedBy: Laurel wants the replacement to be real, and Floyd is the man she takes in; the reader is fooled the same way.

storyboard.claim: Laurel is so desperate for the copy to be real that she is fooled.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Laurel, sad and slumped, beside Floyd with a smirk that reads as the man who holds the lie.
storyboard.onScreenText: Desperate for the copy to be real
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From the general replacements to the specific pairing of Laurel and Floyd.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows Laurel's need and Floyd's edge; no act of harm is staged.

shotIntent.subject: the gallery walk through ten portraits
shotIntent.action: a route walks from portrait to portrait and ends where two portraits meet
shotIntent.payoff: the plot lives only where two portraits touch

explainedBy: The story is walked like a gallery of ten portraits; the plot appears where two portraits touch.

storyboard.claim: The video walks through ten portraits; the plot is where two touch.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A route of stations from Portrait 1 to Portrait 10, ending at a station marked 'Where two touch'.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Turns from the replacement idea to the structure of the video.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the walk as a route and marks where the plot will appear.

shotIntent.subject: the first portrait, Ellie
shotIntent.action: a chapter card opens Portrait 1 with the date May 2005
shotIntent.payoff: the gallery walk begins with Ellie

explainedBy: Portrait one is Ellie in May 2005, the girl the narrator steps into.

storyboard.claim: Portrait one is Ellie, May 2005.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A broadsheet chapter card: PORTRAIT 1 · ELLIE, May 2005.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Opens the first portrait of the gallery just announced.
storyboard.addedInformation: Names the portrait and its date.

explainedBy: Ellie's core motivation is the demand to be perfect so that she can match Theo.
Being the family's golden girl is a crushing weight for a teenager to carry.

storyboard.claim: The pressure on Ellie is suffocating for a teenager.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Ellie slumped with a worried face, carrying the family's expectations on her own body.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From her demand to be perfect to the pressure that demand puts on her.
storyboard.addedInformation: The pressure is shown on Ellie herself; the narration names it, no object stands for it.

kineticManifesto.footnote: An act put on for others

shotIntent.subject: Ellie's flawless existence
shotIntent.action: 'she is flawless' is struck through and replaced by 'she performs flawless'
shotIntent.payoff: her perfection is a performance, not a fact

explainedBy: Ellie actively performs a flawless existence; it is an act, not who she is.

storyboard.claim: Ellie is performing a flawless existence.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Type: 'SHE IS FLAWLESS' struck through, then 'SHE PERFORMS FLAWLESS'.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Turns the crushing weight into the performance she puts on.
storyboard.addedInformation: The strike-through says the flawlessness is an act.

explainedBy: Theo Goodman is the best-looking boy in Ellie's London school.

balanceScale.title: ELLIE WEIGHS HERSELF
balanceScale.verdict: Her fear sets the tragedy moving

shotIntent.subject: Ellie's fear of being unworthy of Theo
shotIntent.action: Theo's qualities pile on one pan, Ellie's fear of falling short drops on the other
shotIntent.payoff: the fear outweighs everything and becomes the catalyst

explainedBy: Ellie is obsessed with Theo and terrified she is not clever enough for him; that terror starts the tragedy.

storyboard.claim: Ellie's terror of being unworthy of Theo is the catalyst.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A scale: Theo's qualities on the left, Ellie's fear of being unworthy on the right, tipping toward the fear.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From Theo's description to how Ellie measures herself against him.
storyboard.addedInformation: Names the fear as the catalyst of the tragedy.

shotIntent.subject: Ellie's flawless facade
shotIntent.action: the facade passes into the tragedy and its damage
shotIntent.payoff: other people pay for her facade

explainedBy: Ellie's flawless facade sets the tragedy in motion, and its collateral damage falls on others

storyboard.claim: The facade is the catalyst; its damage falls on others.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Three torn-paper notes joined by arrows: facade, tragedy, collateral damage
storyboard.onScreenText: Flawless facade -> The tragedy begins -> Collateral damage
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From Ellie's obsession to what it causes
storyboard.addedInformation: The cause chain now ends on the people hurt

explainedBy: The facade does not stay private; it radiates outward and hurts everyone around Ellie.

storyboard.claim: The facade creates a ripple effect on everyone near her.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The same flow with one more label, Everyone around her.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Adds the effect: the facade's damage reaches the people around her.
storyboard.addedInformation: Only the ripple the narration states; no specific victim is named here.

explainedBy: Insisting on perfection at any cost makes Ellie walk blindly into a trap.

storyboard.claim: Ellie walks blindly into a trap because of her insistence on perfection.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The same flow with one more label, Walks into a trap.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Adds the step where the facade leads Ellie into the trap.
storyboard.addedInformation: The trap is named as the narration names it; its nature is not shown.

explainedBy: Laurel is left in the uncertainty of Ellie's absence, to rot there for a decade.

storyboard.claim: Ellie's absence leaves her mother in uncertainty.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Laurel with a worried face, slumped, alone on stage.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Ends the flow on its result: the mother who is left behind.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows Laurel's state, not the crime; no harm is staged.

shotIntent.subject: the date of the first fracture
shotIntent.action: a rail scrubs back from May 2005 to January 2005 and marks the crack
shotIntent.payoff: the trouble starts months before May

explainedBy: The first real crack in the facade comes in January 2005.

storyboard.claim: The facade first breaks in January 2005.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A timeline rail: January 2005 'The facade cracks', May 2005 'Ellie's portrait'.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Turns from the consequences back to the first event, in January.
storyboard.addedInformation: Places the fracture on a dated rail before the portrait date.

explainedBy: On a bleak winter day, Ellie comes into the family home in a rush of teenage anger.
Ellie drops her rucksack, and Laurel is standing at the kitchen sink.

shotIntent.subject: Ellie's B+ on a maths test
shotIntent.action: a full-bleed split sets the grade itself against what it means to Ellie
shotIntent.payoff: a near-good grade feels like the end of the world to her

explainedBy: A B+ is barely a failure, but to Ellie it is the end of the world.

storyboard.claim: A B+ feels like the end of the world to Ellie.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A full-bleed split: left 'The grade: B+', right 'To Ellie: The end of the world'.
storyboard.onScreenText: B+ / The end of the world
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From her complaint in the hallway to the grade behind it.
storyboard.addedInformation: Sets the grade against Ellie's reading of it side by side.

explainedBy: Ellie insists she will fail her GCSEs, exams that dictate a British teenager's future.
Laurel is aware of the family's tight finances when she suggests cheaper help.
noVisual: Laurel at the family kitchen table, worried about money; the finances are said, not drawn

shotIntent.subject: Laurel's cheaper options for help
shotIntent.action: two cheap branches grow from 'help Ellie with maths' and are both pruned

explainedBy: Laurel suggests cheaper help, and Ellie refuses it outright.

storyboard.claim: Ellie rejects Laurel's cheaper suggestions.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A tree: 'Help Ellie with maths' branches to maths club and a sixth former for pounds and cake; both pruned.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From Laurel's finances to the refusal that answers her.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows both cheap options and that each is cut off.

explainedBy: Ellie pushes her mother for a professional tutor and offers her own pocket money.

storyboard.claim: Ellie demands a real tutor and offers her own pocket money.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Ellie angry, pointing at her mother, who stands worried in the kitchen.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From the refusal to the pressure: the demand becomes a push.
storyboard.addedInformation: The pointing gesture is the demand; the pocket money is named only in the callout.

shotIntent.subject: Ellie's hidden insecurity
shotIntent.action: the false reason is struck through

explainedBy: The outburst is not about the maths teacher; it hides Ellie's fear of not being good enough for Theo

storyboard.claim: The outburst hides Ellie's fear of not being good enough for Theo.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Bold lines of type; 'About the maths teacher' is struck through
storyboard.onScreenText: Not good enough for Theo; About the maths teacher (struck)
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From her demand for a tutor to what drives it
storyboard.addedInformation: The struck line shows the false reading of the outburst

explainedBy: The outburst is really about the fear of the mask slipping and of being fundamentally flawed.

storyboard.claim: Ellie fears being fundamentally flawed.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Ellie standing still, her face now afraid.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Keeps the same stage and turns the worried face into fear of being flawed.
storyboard.addedInformation: Fear replaces worry on the same stage; nothing new is added.

stackReveal.title: WHAT SHE HIDES
stackReveal.subtitle: Layer under layer
stackReveal.callout: The fear under the perfect surface

shotIntent.subject: the fear Ellie hides
shotIntent.action: a cutaway reveals layer after layer under 'perfect grades'
shotIntent.payoff: at the bottom: no longer the prize Theo deserves

explainedBy: Ellie fears that if she slips academically she will no longer be the prize Theo deserves.

storyboard.claim: Ellie fears losing her place as Theo's prize.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A strata cutaway: perfect grades, fear of slipping, the illusion shatters, no longer the prize.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From the mask slipping to the loss she fears.
storyboard.addedInformation: Orders the hidden fear as layers down to the prize.

shotIntent.subject: Laurel's view of Ellie
shotIntent.action: the borderless split sets what Laurel sees against what Ellie hides
shotIntent.payoff: Laurel sees only a flawless, ambitious child

explainedBy: Laurel, at the sink, sees only a flawless, ambitious child, not the fear Ellie hides.

storyboard.claim: Laurel sees Ellie only as flawless and ambitious.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Split: 'Laurel sees: flawless, ambitious' against 'Ellie hides: fear of slipping'.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From Ellie's hidden fear to her mother's blind spot.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the gap between Laurel's view and Ellie's reality.

explainedBy: Laurel's perception is blinded by the glow of her youngest daughter, so she misses the panic.

storyboard.claim: Laurel is blinded by the glow of her daughter.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Laurel with a neutral face, standing in the kitchen.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From the flawless child to the blindness that causes Laurel to miss the panic.
storyboard.addedInformation: The blindness is the narration's word; no icon reads it, so the callout carries it.

shotIntent.subject: Laurel's view of Ellie
shotIntent.action: the scale tips toward 'a dedicated student' over 'consuming panic'
shotIntent.payoff: Laurel sees only ambition, not the panic

explainedBy: Laurel sees a dedicated student who wants to excel, not a consuming panic.

storyboard.claim: Laurel sees a dedicated student, not the panic.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A balance tipping to 'A dedicated student' (she sees) over 'Consuming panic' (she misses).
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Restates the mother's blindness as a weighing.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows what she sees outweighing what she misses.

explainedBy: Laurel gives in to Ellie's demand and hires the tutor, while Ellie is pleased.

storyboard.claim: Laurel gives in to the demand for a tutor.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Laurel sad and holding still beside Ellie, who looks happy.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: From the pressure to the answer: the mother gives in.
storyboard.addedInformation: Laurel's sadness is the cost of yielding; Ellie's happiness is the result she gets.

explainedBy: The fatal consequence of yielding arrives a few months later, in May 2005.
